statement: A quaternion is an element of a four-dimensional number system with four real-number components, expressible in the form q = a + b*i + c*j + d*k = a + v (or as a pair of complex numbers (a + b*i) + (c + d*i)*j in C^2), equipped with addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, where multiplication is associative, distributive, and non-commutative, governed by j^2 = -1 and i*j = -j*i = k.

properties.property: Quaternion multiplication is non-commutative (the product depends on the order of the factors)
properties.why: The imaginary basis elements satisfy anticommutative relations such as i*j = -j*i

properties.property: Quaternions can be represented as pairs of complex numbers (Cayley–Dickson construction)
properties.why: Writing a vector in C^2 in basis {1, j} as (a + b*i)1 + (c + d*i)j with j^2 = -1 and i*j = -j*i = k produces the quaternion multiplication rules

properties.property: Quaternions admit 48 distinct 4x4 real matrix representations in M(4, R)
properties.why: Sum and product operations are preserved under homomorphism into quadruples of matrices consisting of a scalar identity matrix and three skew-symmetric matrices

properties.property: The equation q^2 = -1 has infinitely many solutions forming a unit 2-sphere in R^3
properties.why: Setting (a + b*i + c*j + d*k)^2 = -1 forces the scalar part a = 0 and b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = 1

properties.property: Quaternions admit an exponential and polar decomposition q = ||q|| * exp(n_hat * phi) = ||q|| * (cos(phi) + n_hat * sin(phi))
properties.why: The power series exp(q) = sum_{n=0}^infty q^n / n! separates into scalar e^a * cos(||v||) and unit directional vector (v / ||v||) * sin(||v||)

assumptions.assumption: Components a, b, c, d are real numbers
assumptions.breaks_when: Components are selected from non-real fields or algebraic structures not satisfying real arithmetic

assumptions.assumption: Basis elements satisfy j^2 = -1 and anticommuting relation i*j = -j*i = k
assumptions.breaks_when: Multiplication is assumed commutative, collapsing the structure to commutative algebras or standard complex numbers

failure_modes.cause: Treating quaternion multiplication as commutative when multiplying expressions

failure_modes.mode: Undefined polar direction for scalar quaternions
failure_modes.signature: Division by zero when evaluating v / ||v||
failure_modes.cause: The vector part v has norm 0 (||v|| = 0), requiring an arbitrary choice of unit vector n_hat

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero in computing p^(-1)
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating multiplicative inverse on the zero quaternion where ||q|| = 0
